D006_m001.question:
I’ve been a nurse for over twenty-five years—supervising a busy unit, managing staff, keeping things running. But for the past year or so, things have… slipped. It started with sleeping less, needing less—only three or four hours, but I didn’t feel tired. I’d stay late at work, reorganize charts, start new protocols, delegate tasks—I couldn’t sit still. Little noises would snap my attention—a pen dropping, a page turning—and I’d jump in to fix something that didn’t need fixing.

But then the voices started. At first, I thought it was staff whispering, but there was no one there. They tell me I’m corrupting the unit, that my blood is poisoned, turning black. That’s when I started checking my arms, my pulse—nothing, but I *know* something’s wrong internally. My husband says I’m not making sense, that I’ll start a sentence about staffing and end up talking about satellites watching the hospital.

For a while, I couldn’t leave the house. I’d stand on the balcony and get this sudden urge—to step forward, just let go. Didn’t plan it, but the pull was real. Now the highs and lows keep crashing into each other. The voices don’t stop, even when I’m not manic. They’ve been there longer than the sadness, longer than the racing—I still hear them when I’m quiet. That can’t just be mood, can it?
